saints.name: St. Patrick
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: Carried off to Ireland as a slave and returning as its bishop, he won a nation to Christ and left behind his own Confession of God’s mercy…
biography: Born in Roman Britain late in the fourth century, Patrick was the son of Calpurnius, a deacon and town councillor, and the grandson of the priest Potitus. Seized by Irish raiders at sixteen, he herded flocks in slavery for six years, learning to pray without ceasing, before escaping to a ship some two hundred miles away.

After years of study in Gaul he returned to Ireland as a bishop — tradition dates his mission from 432 — baptizing thousands, ordaining clergy, and contending with kings and druids. Two of his writings survive: the Confessio, his account of God's mercy to him, and a letter excommunicating the soldiers of Coroticus, who had slain and enslaved his new converts.

He died, by the commonly received account, in 461 and is buried at Downpatrick. As the apostle who won Ireland to Christ he is its chief patron; the later legends that he drove the snakes from the island and taught the Trinity with a shamrock still cling to his memory.
saints.knownFor: The evangelization of Ireland; the Confessio; the “Breastplate” prayer attributed to him.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 17 March
